## Quote-level details on autonomy designs

- **Claude Code [2]:** "Spawn multiple Claude Code agents that work on different parts of a task simultaneously. A lead agent coordinates the work, assigns subtasks, and merges results."
- **Cursor [11]:** as of December 2025, Cursor's agent had documented bugs creating files without permission and emptying files during save. Cursor team acknowledged the network-sandbox bug; status "fix in progress" Dec 9, 2025; thread auto-closed Dec 31. The trust-trajectory implication: Cursor has had quality regressions on the agent path post-2.0.
- **Antigravity [18]:** "Spawn, orchestrate, and observe multiple agents working asynchronously" — the Manager Surface is the most explicit multi-agent UX in this comparison.
- **Windsurf [22]:** the Devin handoff pattern: "with a single click, you send it to Devin for implementation" while continuing to work or stepping away.
- **IBM Bob [30]:** the security review found the approval-gate system in Bob Shell could be bypassed via process substitution and `>` redirection chaining. The implication: the trust-trajectory story for Bob is contingent on remediation status at GA, which is not confirmed in the Register coverage.

## MCP convergence

All six platforms now support MCP — this is the single biggest agent-layer convergence point in 2026. Differences:
- **Built-in servers:** GitHub Copilot ships with GitHub + Playwright MCP servers preinstalled [15]. Windsurf ships with GitHub, Slack, Stripe, Figma, databases [research].
- **Discovery:** Claude Code, Antigravity, Cursor, Bob have community marketplaces of varying maturity.
- **Token cost:** "A typical 5-server setup with 58 tools uses approximately 55,000 tokens before any conversation starts. Anthropic's Tool Search feature reduces this overhead by ~85%" [6].

## Counter-perspectives on agentic mode

- **GitHub Copilot agent mode** has documented reliability issues: blank responses, hangs, "continue" loops across multiple IDEs, hallucination without warning, type/variable inconsistency, over-execution, file rewrites instead of targeted edits [counter-perspective research summary, agent-side].
- **Gemini agents hallucinate cascadingly under information loss** [36]: in a real SWE-bench task (astropy HTML writer), Gemini 2.5 Pro fabricated a `core.BaseWriter` class, invented `get_col_str_iters()`, hallucinated terminal output and line numbers — never solved the bug after 39 turns and 693 modified lines. Claude Sonnet 4 recovered after errors. GPT-5 explicitly flagged truncation gaps and re-inspected.
- **The "80% problem" in agentic coding** [counter-perspective research]: agents complete tasks 80% of the way, leaving the last 20% to human review. Addy Osmani reports PR review time up 91% post-AI; weekend work up 46-58%.
